paragraphs: Adler University is a graduate-only institution rooted in the philosophy of Alfred Adler, who believed that individual health and well-being are inseparable from that of the community. Founded in Chicago in 1952 by Rudolf Dreikurs, a psychiatrist and advocate of Adlerian psychology, the university opened its Vancouver campus in 2005, making it one of the few psychology-focused graduate universities with a dedicated Canadian presence.

The Vancouver campus offers master and doctoral programs in counselling and clinical psychology, including the M.A. and MCP in Counselling Psychology, specializations in Art Therapy and School and Youth counselling, and the rigorous five-year Psy.D. in Clinical Psychology. Programs are available in full-time and part-time formats, blending academic study with extensive clinical practica through more than 700 community partner organizations.

Adler University distinguishes itself through its social justice mission. Students collectively provide hundreds of thousands of community service hours each year, partnering with underserved populations through initiatives like Adler Community Health Services. The Vancouver campus works closely with Indigenous communities and emphasizes culturally responsive, equity-focused practice in psychology and counselling.

International students are welcome at the Vancouver campus, with applications accepted for both Fall (deadline May 1) and Spring (deadline September 1) terms. The university offers a range of merit and need-based scholarships specifically for Vancouver students, including the Entrance Merit Scholarship of up to CA$7,500, the Indigenous Student Scholarship, and awards for Psy.D. candidates. Programs are approved by the British Columbia Ministry of Advanced Education.
